name: Brenipatide
summary: Brenipatide (LY3537031) is Lilly's wholly owned dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist, given as a subcutaneous injection, being developed for psychiatric and addiction disorders. The lead Phase 3 programme is RENEW-MDD-1 (NCT07412756, 1,000 participants, primary completion 2028-02) and RENEW-MDD-2 (NCT07775300, 1,000 participants, primary completion 2028-12): adjunctive brenipatide added to stable standard care versus placebo, with time to relapse of MDD as the primary endpoint. No human efficacy data in depression has been published. Price anchor: Vraylar (cariprazine), the branded adjunctive-MDD comparator the book carries, at $9,662 CMS Part D spend per beneficiary in 2024. Uptake anchor: Auvelity, the newest MDD-only brand with a clean CMS series, which captured 0.23% a year of the untreated, treated-for-depression Medicare Part D pool in its second full year.

therapy_mode.source: NCT07412756 and NCT07775300 (ClinicalTrials.gov): adjunctive treatment, with time to relapse as the primary endpoint, so the use is long-term maintenance
therapy_mode.note: A relapse-prevention label implies continuous dosing alongside the patient's antidepressant

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Vraylar: CMS Part D 2024, $1,135,973,310 spend over 117,573 beneficiaries = $9,662 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: JUDGEMENT on the choice of comparator. Vraylar holds an adjunctive MDD label (approved December 2022), the same setting as the RENEW trials, and the book carries its demand. Caplyta, which holds the same adjunctive-MDD label (November 2025), comes in at $9,940 per beneficiary in 2024 and supports the anchor. The case against it: Vraylar's Medicare spend is mostly schizophrenia and bipolar use, and Lilly may price an incretin at the class level instead: Mounjaro $7,084, Ozempic $6,642 per beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand). That price would be about 27% lower. Rexulti, the most-used adjunctive-MDD brand, is not in the book's demand table

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention: halving a CMS per-beneficiary figure lands at a median 96% of CMS's own negotiated net prices (retatrutide seed, backend/gross_to_net.py)
gross_to_net_pct.note: Net is 50% of list. Cross-check: Vraylar's IPAY 2027 maximum fair price is $770 per 30 days (book negotiated_prices, cms_mfp), which is about $9,370 for a full year. That is well above half the $9,662 part-year CMS figure, so for this comparator the convention may overstate the discount. It is kept because the two bases differ: per-beneficiary spend covers part of a year, and the MFP is a full-year price

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the stock per year
discontinuation_pct.source: reused from the retatrutide seed: GLP-1 discontinuation at 1 year in adults with overweight or obesity and no type 2 diabetes, 64.8% (JAMA Network Open, Jan 2025, 125,474 adults, US EHR data 2018-2023)
discontinuation_pct.note: JUDGEMENT to reuse it. The same incretin class carries the same GI tolerability burden and injection burden. Case against: this is an obesity population, not a depressed population on stable antidepressants, and a relapse-prevention label may keep patients on drug longer. Antidepressant persistence is also poor, so the direction of the error is not clear

forecast_start_year.source: primary completion dates in the book's trials table: NCT07412756 2028-02, NCT07775300 2028-12 (both estimated)
forecast_start_year.note: JUDGEMENT. A launch after 2027 is clear. The second relapse trial reads out at end-2028, a filing follows in 2029, and a standard review puts a US launch in late 2029 or 2030, so 2030 is the first full year. Case against: an earlier first approval in alcohol use disorder (Phase 3 readout expected mid-2028, per Psychiatric Times) could bring the molecule to market sooner, but MDD use would still need the MDD label

exus_multiple.source: reused from the retatrutide seed: tirzepatide's filed FY2025 molecule-level split, 9,373mm ex-US against 27,135mm US (LLY 10-K 0000059478-26-000013)
exus_multiple.note: JUDGEMENT. It uses Lilly's own incretin footprint. Case against: the psychiatric comparators are essentially US-only products (Vraylar, Auvelity), and ex-US payers price adjunctive antidepressants low, so the ratio for this indication could be well below 0.35

economics_share.source: Lilly-coded molecule (LY3537031), sponsored by Eli Lilly and Company on every listed trial (context file); no partner is named in any source found

prevalence.source: carried by the book: epidemiology.csv, 21,414,000 (NIMH/NSDUH, 8.3% of US adults with a past-year major depressive episode)
prevalence.note: The book fills it, so no second figure is set

incidence.source: carried by the book (epidemiology.csv row, incidence blank)

eligible_pct.source: NIMH, Major Depression statistics (nimh.nih.gov/health/statistics/major-depression), from NSDUH 2021: 61.0% of US adults with a past-year major depressive episode received treatment
eligible_pct.note: The label is adjunctive to stable standard care (RENEW-MDD-1 inclusion requires stable MDD standard-of-care medication), so it reaches the treated. This is an upper bound: 'treatment' includes talk therapy alone, and the medication-only share could not be sourced. Exclusions (psychosis, bipolar disorder, eating disorders, type 1 diabetes) are small against the pool

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the untreated eligible pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: Auvelity, CMS Part D (lookup.py demand Auvelity): 9,268 beneficiaries in 2023, 16,448 in 2024. Pool: 53.1mm Part D enrollees in 2024 (KFF, Key Facts About Medicare Part D Enrollment 2024) x 17.54% with depressive disorders (CMS Chronic Conditions Warehouse, 2022, fee-for-service) x 61.0% treated = 5,681,381. New patients in 2024 = 16,448 - 9,268 x (1 - 0.648) = 13,186, over the 5,672,113 untreated = 0.2325%
penetration_peak_pct.note: JUDGEMENT: a 1.0x multiple on Auvelity, the most recent MDD-only branded launch with a clean CMS series. Arguments for a higher peak: this is Auvelity's second full year, not its peak (Axsome reported FY2025 net sales of $507.1mm, up 74%, and Q4 2025 prescriptions up 42% year on year), and an incretin's weight-loss effect may help uptake. Arguments for a lower peak: the label is adjunctive relapse prevention only, it is an injectable, and Auvelity's 2024 rate is a Medicare rate applied to the whole US pool. The 64.8% discontinuation used in the solve is the same as the asset field

ramp_steepness.source: Auvelity CMS Part D beneficiaries, 9,268 in 2023 to 16,448 in 2024, a step of 1.775x, so k = ln(1.775) = 0.574
ramp_steepness.note: JUDGEMENT. It treats the series as still in its early exponential phase, which understates k if Auvelity had already begun to bend. No MDD competitor is modelled in the book. The incretin curve in the retatrutide seed (k 1.402, from Mounjaro) was rejected: psychiatric launches ramp more slowly, and Auvelity grew 1.77x in its second full year where Mounjaro grew 2.42x

ramp_midpoint_year.source: Axsome FY2025 results (8-K, February 2026): Auvelity net sales up 74% in its third full year, with Q4 2025 prescriptions up 42% year on year and 8% quarter on quarter
ramp_midpoint_year.note: JUDGEMENT. Auvelity was still growing fast in year three but slowing (8% quarter on quarter), which puts its half-of-peak point around year 3. Case against: this rests on one launch, and a relapse-prevention adjunct could build more slowly
